confidentialite.intro: The Ultra Tour de la Ria association attaches great importance to the protection of your personal data. This privacy policy informs you about how your data is collected and used.
confidentialite.controllerBody:
The data controller is:

Ultra Tour de la Ria association

11 rue de l'Éolienne, 56510 Saint-Pierre-Quiberon, France

Email: contact@ultratourdelaria.fr
confidentialite.dataBody: This showcase website does not collect any personal data directly. There is no contact form or newsletter sign-up, and the site itself does not set any tracking cookies. The race pages do, however, embed a map provided by Strava (see the "Third-party content" section).
confidentialite.registrationBody:
Registration for the Ultra Tour de la Ria is handled by the Klikego platform. When you register for the event, your personal data is collected and processed by Klikego in accordance with their own privacy policy. We invite you to review Klikego's terms when you register.



The registration data passed on to the Ultra Tour de la Ria association is used solely to organise the event: bib management, race-related communication, results, etc.
confidentialite.embedsBody: The race pages display the routes using a map module provided by Strava (strava-embeds.com), which relies on the Mapbox mapping service. When you visit these pages, your browser loads resources from these services' servers, which then receive technical data such as your IP address and may set their own cookies. This processing is governed by the privacy policies of Strava and Mapbox, which we invite you to consult.
confidentialite.cookiesBody: This site does not set tracking or advertising cookies. Essential technical cookies may be used by the host (GitHub Pages), and the Strava map modules embedded in the race pages may set their own cookies (see the "Third-party content" section).

patrimoine.title: Natural heritage

entrainement.title: Training
entrainement.text: Whether you're aiming to finish your trail or chase a personal best, here's all the advice you need to be at your peak on race day. We also offer a personal coach!

entrainementPage.heroAlt: A blur of runners in motion
entrainementPage.introTitle: Preparation is what gets you to the finish line. Here is everything we know, and everything the coach knows
entrainementPage.introText1: Whether you are after a training plan, nutrition advice or simply want to know what is waiting for you at each aid station, it is all on this page.
entrainementPage.introText2: No excuse for a bad race day!
entrainementPage.coachText1: Born in Landévant, one of the villages the course runs through, Ronan Kervadec has known these trails since he was a child.
entrainementPage.coachText2: A trail and triathlon coach, he can guide you whether you want to finish or to race hard. He also offers coaching packages built around you, with training that evolves as you do.
entrainementPage.coachAlt: Portrait of Ronan Kervadec, trail and triathlon coach
entrainementPage.ravitosIntro: Every aid station has what you need to carry on in the best possible shape.
entrainementPage.ravitosSecDesc: Fruit, energy bars, gels, dried fruit
entrainementPage.ravitosMapAlt: Course map showing the aid stations
entrainementPage.nutritionCadence: Then keep the same rhythm all the way to the finish.
entrainementPage.nutritionPhotoAlt: Two trail runners climbing a forest path
entrainementPage.nutritionRationChaque: At every marker: 400‑500 mL drink + 1 gel
entrainementPage.nutritionPhoto2Alt: Backlit moss and grasses on the forest floor
entrainementPage.materielIntro: You must carry certain gear and enough food for the whole race. Here is the list — spot checks do happen.
entrainementPage.materielTelephoneDetail: race HQ number saved, flight mode not allowed
entrainementPage.materielFrontaleDetail: on the relay, for the first runner
entrainementPage.materielEauDetail: 1 L minimum on the 80 km, 0.5 L on the 33 km and the relay
entrainementPage.materielCaniculeIntro: The organisers can make it compulsory the day before. You will get a text message.
entrainementPage.materielIntemperies: In severe weather the organisers may also require extra gear, announced by text a few days before.
entrainementPage.materielGlisser: Swipe the table to see all three races.
entrainementPage.reglesIntro: As a runner you also have a part to play in protecting this place. Breaking these rules can get you disqualified, so keep your eyes open.
entrainementPage.reglesDechetsTexte: Even biodegradable waste stays with you until the next aid station.
entrainementPage.reglesBalisageTexte: Never cut through the vegetation. The paths are marked the way they are to protect fragile habitats.
entrainementPage.reglesPrivesTexte: The course crosses private property in places. Stay on the marked route and do not stray from it.
entrainementPage.reglesBiodiversiteTexte: Do not pick plants and do not disturb the animals — you are running through their home.

coaching.heroAlt: Ronan Kervadec with his arms out at a race finish
coaching.bio1: With training that is built properly you will arrive physically ready, you will cut your risk of injury and you will handle your effort and your nutrition better. You will be more confident and calmer on the start line.
coaching.bio2Avant: Long distances are my home ground: I have raced
coaching.bio2Fort: the Ultra-Marin several times, over distances from 34 km to 100 km
coaching.bio2Apres: — courses very close to what the Ultra Tour de la Ria has in store.
coaching.altTriathlon: Ronan Kervadec in a triathlon suit, wearing a sun hat
coaching.altTrail: Ronan Kervadec trail running with poles in the mountains
coaching.altGroupe: Ronan Kervadec running in a pack on a bridge
coaching.faqQ3a: Nutrition is a huge part of a good race. For efforts lasting several hours, current guidance sits somewhere between 45 and 90 g of carbohydrate an hour, depending on your level and on what your stomach tolerates.
coaching.faqQ3b: But nutrition is something you rehearse in training, especially on your long runs. What you eat is personal: some prefer liquid (sports drink), some semi-liquid (gels, fruit purée), some solid (bars, chews). Test it all in training.
coaching.faqQ4: Should you train on the course itself?
coaching.faqQ5: What are the most common mistakes?
coaching.offresContenu: Three to six running sessions plus one general conditioning session. Three to twelve hours of training a week.
coaching.offre1PlanSousTitre: Built around your goal and your race
coaching.offre2Plan1: Online questionnaire and a call before the coaching starts
coaching.offre2Plan2: Message your coach, answer within 24 hours
coaching.offre2Plan5: A weekly individualised plan that can be adjusted
coaching.offre2Plan6: Access to a coaching and performance-tracking app (iDO Sport)
coaching.offresPrixNote: if you have bought a race entry
coaching.conseil1: The Ultra de la Ria asks a lot of you, but it is also quite an adventure. Train seriously, build up gradually…
coaching.conseil2: and above all enjoy it, during the months of training as much as on race day.
coaching.conseilAlt: Runners' legs blurred with motion over grass
coaching.contactTexte: A question about the plans or about your own training? Drop me a line and I will get back to you.
coaching.offresAlt: A runner blurred with motion on the road
coaching.faqQ1a: Count on twelve to sixteen weeks of specific training before race day, starting from an endurance base you already have. For the 80 km, aim for the upper end; for the 33 km, ten to twelve weeks are enough if you already run regularly.
coaching.faqQ1b: The point is not to pile on big weeks from the start. You build up gradually, with an easier week roughly every third week, and you finish with a two-week taper where the volume drops right back.
coaching.faqQ2a: Three to six running sessions depending on your level and the time you have, plus one general conditioning session. Three well-placed sessions beat five done half-heartedly.
coaching.faqQ2b: The weekend long run matters most: that is where you build endurance and where you test your kit and your nutrition. The rest of the week keeps things ticking over and adds a little intensity.
coaching.faqQ4a: It is not essential, but it helps a lot. The course mixes coastal paths, tracks and faster, flatter stretches, and walking or running some of it beforehand saves you from nasty surprises.
coaching.faqQ4b: If you live far away, look for outings with a similar profile: short, repeated climbs rather than long ascents, on soft ground. Recceing one or two key stretches, the finish especially, is usually enough to settle your nerves.
coaching.faqQ5a: Going out too fast, first of all. The opening kilometres feel easy and you pay dearly for them later. Then neglecting to drink and eat in the first two hours: once the fatigue arrives it is too late to catch up.
coaching.faqQ5b: And trying something new on race day. Shoes, pack, a gel you have never taken — everything you wear and everything you swallow should have been tested in training. Do not skimp on sleep the week before either; it counts for more than one last big session.
coaching.philo1Suite: the runner in front of me
coaching.philo2Suite: there is no way around them over long distances
coaching.philo3Fort: Add speed on top of solid endurance
coaching.philo3Suite: so you can race at the level you are after

course.altMateriel: Trail runner's gear laid flat: vest, map, poles, shoes and bib
course.riaText: is one of Brittany's natural jewels. This former river valley flooded by the sea is home to remarkable biodiversity: migratory birds, fish, shellfish and unique flora.
course.altVueAerienne: Aerial view of the Ria d'Étel and its sandbar
course.prepareText: Whether you're aiming to finish your trail or chase a personal best, here's all the advice you need to be at your peak on race day. We also offer a personal coach!

course80.heroAlt: Ultra 80 km runner wearing a cap and hydration vest
course80.infoTitle: The full tour of the Ria d'Étel, a semi-self-sufficient course that will awaken the trail runner within you
course80.description: The 80 km (Tour de la Ria) takes you on a total immersion in Brittany's landscapes, through pine forests, coastal paths and a sea crossing.
course80.hydratationText: 80 km in semi-self-sufficiency: at least 1 L of water in the pack, aid stations every 10 to 15 km. Between them, every runner is on their own.
course80.parcoursLabelText: The full loop of the Ria d'Étel — coastal trails, a protected Natura 2000 site, and a boat crossing with neutralised timing.
course80.equipementsText: Race pack, headlamp, waterproof jacket, survival blanket, whistle, charged phone. Checks may be carried out; poles are forbidden.
course80.entrainementLabelText: 15 hours maximum to complete the loop. Food reserve mandatory — over this distance, preparation makes all the difference.
course80.dossardText: Chip-fitted bib, worn visibly on the front from start to finish. Collection at the salle Émeraude in Locoal-Mendon, ID required.

course33.infoTitle: The Ria 33, an escape blending nature and effort. An adventure that will leave you wanting to go ever further!
course33.description: The 33 km takes you through the Ria d'Étel's most iconic landscapes, alternating between technical trails and breathtaking scenery.
course33.hydratationText: 33 km in semi-self-sufficiency: at least 0.5 L of water, aid stations every 10 to 15 km. Between them, every runner is on their own.
course33.parcoursLabelText: Starting from Sainte-Hélène: coastal paths, woodland and views over the Ria. A protected Natura 2000 site, paint-free course marking.
course33.equipementsText: Waterproof jacket, survival blanket, whistle, personal cup, charged phone. Checks may be carried out; poles are forbidden.
course33.entrainementLabelText: 6 hours maximum to reach the finish. Food reserve mandatory — and solid preparation to enjoy it all the way.
course33.dossardText: Chip-fitted bib, worn visibly on the front from start to finish. Collection at the salle Émeraude in Locoal-Mendon, ID required.

courseRelais.heroAlt: Relay duo standing back to back
courseRelais.infoTitle: Share the adventure as a relay! Experience the Tour de la Ria as a duo, between Locoal-Mendon and Sainte-Hélène
courseRelais.description: The first runner links Locoal-Mendon to Sainte-Hélène, crossing the Ria d'Étel by boat, before handing over to their partner, who completes the loop back to Locoal-Mendon.
courseRelais.hydratationText: The loop as a duo, in semi-self-sufficiency: at least 0.5 L of water, aid stations every 10 to 15 km. Between them, every runner is on their own.
courseRelais.parcoursLabelText: 50 km then 30 km, handover in Sainte-Hélène and a boat crossing with neutralised timing: the full loop of the Ria, as a pair.
courseRelais.equipementsText: Waterproof jacket, survival blanket, whistle, charged phone — and a headlamp for the first runner. Poles are forbidden.
courseRelais.entrainementLabelText: 15 hours maximum for the team. Food reserve mandatory — and preparation is a two-person job.
courseRelais.dossardText: Chip-fitted bibs, worn visibly on the front from start to finish. Collection at the salle Émeraude in Locoal-Mendon, ID required.
